content.value_statement: Mobile wallet integration fails when React Native projects mix incompatible Solana clients or omit required provider and signing details. This skill provides stack-specific patterns for connection, chain data, transactions, message signing, authentication, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Selects Solana Kit or web3.js patterns from the project's existing dependencies.
Configures MobileWalletProvider identity, cluster, endpoint, cache, and crypto polyfills.
Implements wallet connection, disconnection, account display, and cancellation handling.
Reads balances with cluster-aware React Query keys and precise lamport handling.
Builds and confirms mobile wallet transactions with current blockhash and context data.
Guides message signing and Sign-In with Solana payload construction.
limitations: Mobile Wallet Adapter requires an Android development build and does not work in Expo Go.
The skill does not install a wallet application or provide an RPC service.
Backend nonce issuance and signature verification still require server implementation.
Generated transaction flows require project-specific validation, testing, and security review.

use_cases.title: Add Wallet Connection
use_cases.description: Add reliable connect, disconnect, account display, and cancellation states to an Expo application.

use_cases.title: Ship Transaction Flows
use_cases.description: Build SOL transfers or program instructions with fresh blockhash data, wallet signing, and confirmation.

use_cases.title: Secure Wallet Authentication
use_cases.description: Design Sign-In with Solana payloads using nonce, domain, expiration, and backend verification requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a Wallet
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my React Native Expo project and add a wallet connect button using its existing Solana client stack.

prompt_templates.title: Load Wallet Balances
prompt_templates.prompt: Add wallet balance loading with React Query, including cluster-aware cache keys, cancellation handling, and clear disconnected states.

prompt_templates.title: Send and Confirm SOL
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a SOL transfer flow with recipient validation, amount checks, fee handling, fresh blockhash data, confirmation, and user-visible errors.

prompt_templates.title: Design Verified Sign-In
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Sign-In with Solana using a server nonce, domain binding, expiration, signature verification, replay protection, and tests.

output_examples.input: Add a connect button to my Solana Kit Expo app.
output: A provider check confirms the application uses the Solana Kit wallet stack.
The connect control displays the active account and supports disconnection.
Wallet picker cancellation returns to the disconnected state without a failure alert.

output_examples.input: Create a safe SOL transfer workflow for an existing web3.js app.
output: The workflow validates the recipient and amount before wallet interaction.
Each attempt uses a fresh blockhash and matching context slot.
The interface reports submission, confirmation, cancellation, and failure states.

output_examples.input: Plan Sign-In with Solana for protected backend sessions.
output: The backend issues a short-lived, single-use nonce.
The wallet signs a domain-bound payload with issue and expiration times.
The backend verifies the signature, address, nonce, domain, and replay status before creating a session.

best_practices: Inspect package.json before choosing Solana Kit or web3.js, and keep one client stack throughout the application.
Test transaction flows on devnet before mainnet, and show users the recipient, amount, network, and expected fee.
Keep RPC credentials server-side, issue authentication nonces on the server, and verify every wallet signature before granting access.
anti_patterns: Do not mix Solana Kit provider, hook, or transaction patterns with web3.js patterns.
Do not grant backend access from a minimal sign-in payload without nonce, domain, expiration, and server verification.
Do not execute unpinned latest packages or overwrite a fixed temporary path without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Expo Go?
faq.answer: No. Mobile Wallet Adapter requires an Android development build with native dependencies.

faq.question: Which Solana client stack should I use?
faq.answer: Use Solana Kit for new projects. Keep web3.js only when the existing project already depends on it or explicitly requires it.

faq.question: Can the skill connect to mainnet?
faq.answer: Yes, but mainnet requires an explicit RPC URL. Protect paid RPC credentials and test the full flow on devnet first.

faq.question: Does the skill handle wallet authentication?
faq.answer: It constructs Sign-In with Solana payloads. Protected sessions still require server-issued nonces, backend signature verification, and replay prevention.

faq.question: Can it sign and send transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers instruction sending, explicit transaction construction, blockhash lifetime, context slots, fee checks, and confirmation.

faq.question: Does it support iOS?
faq.answer: The documented Mobile Wallet Adapter workflow targets Android. Verify current wallet and protocol support before planning an iOS implementation.
